edges.description: The step from a ubiquitous enzyme deficiency to a cell-type-restricted degeneration is exactly what is not explained for this disease, so the intermediates are recorded as unknown rather than asserted.
Optic atrophy is the visible consequence of retinal ganglion cell and axon loss; the two are the same event seen histologically and on fundoscopy.
Acuity loss follows from degeneration of the papillomacular bundle that carries central vision, which is the intermediate step.
Same papillomacular-bundle intermediate, measured as a field defect rather than as acuity.
Dyschromatopsia follows from loss of the same central axon population, and is characteristically severe in this disorder.

nodes.description: Central or centrocecal scotoma, absolute in the severely affected proband and relative in the papillomacular area in his more mildly affected siblings.

evidence.reference_title: TMEM126A mutation in a Moroccan family with autosomal recessive optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: His visual acuity was <20/400 bilaterally (at age 16), the optic discs showed bilateral pallor (Figure 2), the patient had an absolute central scotoma bilaterally (Figure 3A) and severe dyschromatopsia, the standard electroretinogram was normal, and OCT showed thinning of all RNFL bundles (Figure 4A).

evidence.reference_title: TMEM126A mutation in a Moroccan family with autosomal recessive optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: relative scotoma in the papillomacular area bilaterally

nodes.description: Dyschromatopsia, characteristically severe, and one of the features distinguishing the recessive optic atrophies from OPA1-linked dominant disease.

evidence.reference_title: TMEM126A mutation in a Moroccan family with autosomal recessive optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: At age 16, he presented with sudden bilateral loss of visual acuity and dyschromatopsia.

evidence.reference_title: TMEM126A mutation in a Moroccan family with autosomal recessive optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: They are distinguished from OPA1-linked optic neuropathy by the recessive pattern of inheritance, an earlier age of onset (congenital or before age 3), and a generally more severe presentation (possibly including nystagmus or severe dyschromatopsia)

nodes.description: TMEM126A associates with the newly synthesised mtDNA-encoded ND4 subunit and is needed to build the ND4 distal membrane module of complex I. Its paralogue TMEM126B does the same job for the ND2 module, and the two are not interchangeable, which is why losing one produces a specific assembly failure rather than a general one.

evidence.reference_title: Optic atrophy-associated TMEM126A is an assembly factor for the ND4-module of mitochondrial complex I.
evidence.snippet: Pulse-labeling interaction studies reveal that TMEM126A associates with the newly synthesized mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)-encoded ND4 subunit of complex I. Our findings indicate that TMEM126A is involved in the assembly of the ND4 distal membrane module of complex I.

evidence.reference_title: Optic atrophy-associated TMEM126A is an assembly factor for the ND4-module of mitochondrial complex I.
evidence.snippet: we find that the function of TMEM126A is distinct from its paralogue TMEM126B, which acts in assembly of the ND2-module of complex I

evidence.reference_title: NDUFS3 depletion permits complex I maturation and reveals TMEM126A/OPA7 as an assembly factor binding the ND4-module intermediate.
evidence.snippet: The process of degradation of the complex occurs in a hierarchical and modular fashion in which the ND4 module remains stable and bound to TMEM126A.

nodes.description: Complex I activity falls while the other respiratory chain complexes are spared. This is the same biochemical endpoint as the nuclear complex I deficiency disorders and as LHON, reached from a different direction, and it is where the shared bioenergetic reading of the hereditary optic neuropathies starts.

evidence.reference_title: Optic atrophy-associated TMEM126A is an assembly factor for the ND4-module of mitochondrial complex I.
evidence.snippet: we find that loss of TMEM126A results in an isolated complex I deficiency and that TMEM126A interacts with a number of complex I subunits and assembly factors

nodes.description: Bilateral optic atrophy with temporal or diffuse optic disc pallor, the defining feature. Onset is typically in childhood, sometimes apparent from birth, occasionally not until adolescence.

evidence.reference_title: Nonsense mutation in TMEM126A causing autosomal recessive optic atrophy and auditory neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: To define the phenotype and elucidate the molecular basis for an autosomal recessively inherited optic atrophy and auditory neuropathy in a consanguineous family with two affected children.

nodes.description: Reduced visual acuity, progressive over time. In the family described in detail, both affected siblings had poor vision from birth.

evidence.reference_title: Nonsense mutation in TMEM126A causing autosomal recessive optic atrophy and auditory neuropathy.
evidence.snippet: both affected subjects had poor vision from birth and complained of progressive visual loss over time

nodes.description: Retinal ganglion cells and the optic nerve axons they project degenerate, producing the optic atrophy. Why these cells and not others is not established for TMEM126A specifically; the available explanation is the general one offered across the hereditary optic neuropathies, that retinal ganglion cells are especially susceptible to perturbations of mitochondrial homeostasis. See `discussions`.

evidence.reference_title: Understanding the molecular basis and pathogenesis of hereditary optic neuropathies: towards improved diagnosis and management.
evidence.snippet: A unifying feature in the pathophysiology of these disorders appears to involve mitochondrial dysfunction, suggesting that the retinal ganglion cells and their axons are especially susceptible to perturbations in mitochondrial homoeostasis.

evidence.reference_title: The top 10 most frequently involved genes in hereditary optic neuropathies in 2186 probands.
evidence.snippet: Hereditary optic neuropathies are caused by the degeneration of retinal ganglion cells whose axons form the optic nerves

nodes.description: Biallelic TMEM126A variants remove a mitochondrial inner membrane protein. The founder allele is a nonsense variant and the second reported allele is a splice-donor change producing an exon-skipped functional null, so the reported spectrum is dominated by complete loss rather than by hypomorphic change.

evidence.reference_title: TMEM126A is a mitochondrial located mRNA (MLR) protein of the mitochondrial inner membrane.
evidence.snippet: TMEM126A mRNAs are strongly enriched in the vicinity of mitochondria and encode an inner mitochondrial membrane associated cristae protein.

evidence.reference_title: TMEM126A, encoding a mitochondrial protein, is mutated in autosomal-recessive nonsyndromic optic atrophy.
evidence.snippet: TMEM126A is conserved in higher eukaryotes and encodes a transmembrane mitochondrial protein of unknown function, supporting the view that mitochondrial dysfunction may be a hallmark of inherited optic neuropathies including isolated autosomal-recessive forms.
